brief: BofA's Benjamin Bowler derivatives team (Global Equity Volatility Insights, "The Age of Idiosyncratic Risk") finds single-stock vol elevated relative to index vol. 3-month ATM weighted-average stock vol is 38% for the SPX Top 50, about 2.5x index vol, and 31% in Europe, about 1.8x the SX5E. European "fragility events" (3-sigma single-stock moves) set a record last year, and 2026 is tracking toward a top-five year. BofA checks whether earnings options price this correctly by comparing implied versus subsequently realised earnings-day vol. In the US, the equal-weighted implied earnings premium sits at its 85th percentile but realised is higher, at the 91st. Cap-weighted, realised is at the 100th percentile against implied's 77th, so underpricing worsens for larger stocks. More than half of names by count, and over two-thirds by market cap, recently realised bigger earnings moves than implied. In Europe the pattern reverses: implied is at the 94th percentile, equal- and cap-weighted, against realised at the 78th and 72nd. Only about a third of stocks moved more than implied. BofA's conclusion: own US megacap earnings optionality, sell or avoid European earnings vol.
